thought.text: The directory ended up nested at `/opt/elasticsearch/elasticsearch-7.17.28`. Let me fix the layout.

reasoning_content:
I see that the Elasticsearch installation is in `/opt/elasticsearch/elasticsearch-7.17.28`, but the symlink at `/opt/es` is pointing to the wrong directory. I need to either update the symlink to point to the correct subdirectory or move the installation folder directly to `/opt/elasticsearch`.

Since `/opt/elasticsearch` is owned by the elastic user, I'll need to either remove the symlink first (which requires root privileges) or work around this as the elastic user. The simplest approach is to delete the symlink and then move the installation directory to the correct location.

action.command:
rm /opt/es && rmdir /opt/elasticsearch && mv /opt/downloads/elasticsearch-7.17.28 /opt/elasticsearch && chown -R elastic:elastic /opt/elasticsearch && ln -sfn /opt/elasticsearch /opt/es && ls /opt/elasticsearch/bin/elasticsearch && cat > /opt/elasticsearch/config/elasticsearch.yml <<'EOF'
cluster.name: index-data-explorer
node.name: node-1
path.data: /opt/elasticsearch/data
path.logs: /opt/elasticsearch/logs
network.host: 127.0.0.1
http.port: 9200
discovery.type: single-node
EOF
chown elastic:elastic /opt/elasticsearch/config/elasticsearch.yml && echo CONFIG_OK
